coupling.rationale: Textbook separation: client routes only see typed view models through server-side queries, the HTTP client, cache and env handling are confined to one server file, components are dumb props-driven renderers, and shared state is the URL. The only tangles are URL-string patterns repeated across components and the Card type's optional flags, which are cosmetic at this size.

abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions track the app's real variation (cards, sections, sortable columns, view models) and stretch to new cases without flag creep — cardsFor's `extra` hook and MoveTable's column table are genuinely reusable. What keeps it from 5 is the duplicated detail-page scaffold (an Items section would copy ~40 lines) and the header/body column duplication inside MoveTable.

findings.issue: homeData re-implements Card construction (species-name lookup, humanized label, spriteUrl, dex ordering) inline instead of reusing cardsFor (model.ts:82-94), so a card-level bug fix such as the default-Pokémon sprite rule must be applied in two places.
findings.suggestion: Extract the {id, name, label, sprite} construction into a single cardOf(speciesMap, pokemonRef) helper used by both cardsFor and homeData (home only adds the extra types field).

findings.issue: The data-guard + NotFound fallback + PageTitle/h1 scaffold is duplicated verbatim in the four detail routes (moves/[name].tsx:18-22, abilities/[name].tsx:15-19, types/[name].tsx:16-20, pokemon/[name].tsx:41-43); a new resource section like Items means copying ~40 lines.
findings.suggestion: Add a tiny wrapper, e.g. <DetailPage data={move} title={(m) => m.title}>{(m) => …}</DetailPage>, that owns the Show/NotFound/title pattern, and let the four routes share it.

findings.issue: Column definitions are declared twice: as COLUMNS (lines 11-19, drives headers and sorting) and as hardcoded <td> cells in the body (lines 52-60); adding or reordering a column requires two edits that must be kept in sync.
findings.suggestion: Render body cells from the same columns() list (map each column to its renderer or row field), so headers and cells share one source of truth.

findings.issue: Search-box state uses a mutable `pushedQuery` capture plus a timer to reconcile typing, URL updates and back/forward navigation; it is the subtlest code in the app and easy to break when extending (e.g. a second debounced control).
findings.suggestion: Isolate the debounce/URL-sync logic in a small useDebouncedParam(key) hook in lib/ so the route only wires it to the input.

findings.issue: Each query's cache key is a hand-written string literal ('home', 'pokemon', 'pokemon-moves', …); a typo or duplicate key would silently share cached data between resources with no error.
findings.suggestion: Derive keys from the wrapper name (e.g. getAbility.name) or centralise them as constants next to the types.

findings.issue: Route URL patterns are hardcoded in several components (PokemonCard.tsx:11, TypeBadge.tsx:23-25, routes/pokemon/[name].tsx:62, routes/types/index.tsx:22), so changing the URL scheme touches many files.
findings.suggestion: Put path builders (pokemonPath(name), typePath(name)) next to the route param types in lib/.

findings.issue: Card carries optional `types` and `hidden` fields that only specific pages populate, making the card's per-context variant implicit and forcing Show-branches in PokemonCard.tsx:18,25.
findings.suggestion: Either document the variants in a comment or model them as an optional `variant: { types?: Ref[]; note?: string }` sub-object so PokemonCard renders one branch.

findings.issue: The search-param coalescing helper (`param`) is duplicated as `gameParam` in routes/pokemon/[name].tsx:14.
findings.suggestion: Move one shared `firstParam(value, fallback)` helper into lib/format.ts or a lib/search.ts.

summary: This is a well-layered SolidStart v2 app: dumb, props-driven components render serializable server-built view models, and every cross-cutting rule (sprites, names, formatting, caching, API base) is confined to one helper or one server file, so most scenarios are one-file changes. The costs are small and specific: Card construction is duplicated between cardsFor and homeData, the detail-page scaffold is copy-pasted across four routes, and MoveTable declares its columns twice. None of it would slow a maintainer down for long, which is why the app sits at a solid 4 rather than 5.
